Fanttik’s rechargeable tool is designed to make everyday household repairs and DIY projects easier, and it does a good job. Verge commerce editor Brandon Widder once called it his go-to electric screwdriver, noting he’s used it to assemble a bed, tighten bike seats, and perform other small- to medium-sized tasks around the house. Beyond being a capable electric screwdriver, the Fanttik also comes equipped with a few extra conveniences. The screwdriver also comes with 16 S2 hardened steel bits, including flathead and Torx bits, all of which fit inside an included magnetic storage case. The rechargeable 2,000mAh battery should handle up to 340 screws on a single charge, too, and it supports USB-C so you can quickly charge it between projects.

title: LG’s budget-friendly B6E OLED TV is up to 50 percent off this weekend
snippet: LG’s B6E was already one of the most affordable OLED TVs you could buy, but it’s an even better deal now that it’s included as part of Best Buy’s la...
fullText:
LG’s B6E was already one of the most affordable OLED TVs you could buy, but it’s an even better deal now that it’s included as part of Best Buy’s latest doorbuster event. Now through the end of today, November 15th, the 55-inch model is 50 percent off, dropping it to an all-time low of $699.99 ($700 off) at Best Buy. If you want a larger 4K set, the 65- and 77-inch models are also discounted, dropping them to $999.99 ($900 off) and $1,499.99 ($1,200 off), respectively.
LG B6E OLED TV

Where to Buy: $1399.99 $699.99 at Best Buy (55-inch) $1899.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (65-inch) $2699.99 $1499.99 at Best Buy (77-inch)
Although it’s not as bright as LG’s pricier C6, the B6E still delivers the excellent contrast and deep blacks OLEDs are often praised for. It’s nearly identical to the standard B6, except it comes with a simpler remote that lacks the motion controls and voice features found on LG’s Magic Remote. It supports Dolby Vision and HDR10 for more lifelike colors and detail in bright and dark scenes, along with Dolby Atmos for more immersive audio. And with Apple AirPlay and Google Cast built in, you can easily stream content from your phone or tablet and access a variety of streaming apps, including Netflix, HBO Max, and YouTube via LG’s webOS platform.





The B6 also offers a lot of features gamers will appreciate. It has a 120Hz refresh rate for modern gaming consoles, which is still plenty fast even if it doesn’t rival the 165Hz refresh rate on the C6. It also offers variable refresh rate support — including Nvidia G-Sync and AMD FreeSync Premium — to help minimize screen tearing. You also get a zippy Alpha 8 Gen 3 AI processor and four HDMI 2.1 ports, making it easy to connect multiple consoles. It may lack some of the more advanced features found on LG’s more premium OLED TVs, but at 50 percent off, the B6 is a great option if you want the benefits of OLED without spending a fortune.

fullText: The strange, wildly tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune have puzzled scientists since NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft explored the planets in the 1980s. New simulations suggest that extreme conditions deep inside these icy giants create unusual electrical properties that could explain their magnetic fields. Remarkably, the models indicate that their magnetic poles could shift by tens of degrees within just a few decades, far faster than Earth's.

title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss

fullText: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk.

fullText: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections. Scientists found that low arginine levels interfere with the immune system's ability to recognize dangerous cells, while increasing arginine intake reduced colon cancer tumors and improved viral infection outcomes in mice. Even more remarkably, giving mice arginine after they contracted influenza helped them recover.

title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
snippet: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found...
fullText: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia. Keeping regular times for sleeping, eating, and other activities may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood, sleep, and overall health.

fullText: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breaking objects that shone with the brightness of a trillion Suns when the Universe was just 670 million years old. Researchers discovered chemical signatures suggesting that coastal dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals relied partly on nutrients originating in the sea. The findings reveal that marine resources traveled through ancient food chains, supplementing the diets of everything from plant-eating dinosaurs to predators.

While one population has remained stable for decades, another has declined by more than 40%, apparently due to a combination of predators, worsening storms, and changing ocean conditions. Even more surprisingly, the tiny Bounty Islands support nearly as many breeding pairs as the Antipodes Islands, despite being 40 times smaller.

fullText: Stanford researchers have discovered that children who struggle persistently with math may have underlying differences in how their brains manage problem-solving strategies. Children with developmental dyscalculia were slower to switch strategies, less responsive to changes in difficulty, and less able to improve their approach over time. Distinct patterns of brain activity were linked to these difficulties and could even predict certain math-related abilities.

title: 5,000-year-old skulls reveal a disturbing secret of ancient Egypt's first kings

fullText: A 5,000-year-old mystery surrounding the tombs of Egypt’s first kings has taken a disturbing turn. Scientists reexamining 46 ancient skulls discovered evidence of potentially fatal head injuries in 18, suggesting that at least 39% of those studied may have been deliberately killed. The findings support a century-old theory that royal attendants were sacrificed when kings died, possibly to serve them in the afterlife.

fullText: A new study suggests that the right kind of exercise could help protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis following ACL surgery. Researchers found that a four-month supervised rehabilitation program improved pain, muscle strength, and quality of life without damaging knee cartilage. The findings challenge fears that exercise worsens injured knees and could transform how patients recover from ACL reconstruction.

fullText: Smiling may not always make you happier, and new research suggests that forcing yourself to smile repeatedly could actually make you feel worse. In a University of Florida study involving more than 1,100 participants, researchers discovered that while a single artificial smile can provide a small mood boost, repeatedly faking smiles can erase that benefit or even reverse it.

fullText: A major study of nearly 1,900 older adults suggests that stopping statins after age 70 may be relatively safe in the short term for people who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke. However, a higher rate of serious cardiovascular events or death during longer follow-up raises questions about the risks of discontinuing these widely prescribed medications.

title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent

fullText: A new study reveals that viral infections may leave behind hidden damage to the immune system long after symptoms disappear. Researchers found that mice recovering from an acute infection experienced lasting changes to their spleens and weakened immune responses, potentially leaving them more vulnerable to future threats. Surprisingly, prior vaccination completely prevented these harmful changes in the mouse model.

fullText: A sweeping analysis of 540 million years of marine fossils has revealed surprising gaps in our understanding of Earth's ancient life. Scientists discovered that some of the greatest opportunities for finding previously unknown species lie in relatively recent geological periods, rather than the distant past. By mapping unexplored fossil-rich regions around the world, researchers have created a powerful tool to guide future excavations.

The breakthrough offers an unprecedented look at quantum behavior and could help unlock a new generation of ultrafast, light-controlled electronics.

title: Superheated magma could fuel towering lava fountains
snippet: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly? Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme h...
fullText: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly? Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme heat inside magma may help explain the difference. Experiments revealed that superheated magma can delay crystal formation for more than eight hours, compared with just 20 minutes in magma that has not been superheated.

title: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue
snippet: Researchers have uncovered a surprising hidden function of a protein that may hold the key to repairing damaged muscles and treating muscular dystrophy. Known f...
fullText: Researchers have uncovered a surprising hidden function of a protein that may hold the key to repairing damaged muscles and treating muscular dystrophy. Known for protecting chromosomes, TRF2 also helps muscle stem cells maintain their identity and regenerate injured tissue. When scientists removed the protein in mice, muscles struggled to repair themselves, and muscular dystrophy progressed dramatically faster.

title: Scientists discover a common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread
snippet: Scientists have uncovered a surprising way that fructose, a sugar commonly found in sweetened foods and drinks, may help aggressive ovarian cancer spread. Resea...
fullText: Scientists have uncovered a surprising way that fructose, a sugar commonly found in sweetened foods and drinks, may help aggressive ovarian cancer spread. Researchers discovered that cancer cells surviving chemotherapy release fructose that weakens the bonds holding neighboring tumor cells together, making it easier for cancer to spread. High dietary fructose levels and cholesterol-lowering statins also produced concerning effects in preclinical experiments.

title: AI supercharges laser physics with a stunning 250x speed boost
snippet: Researchers at Stanford, UCLA, and SLAC have developed an AI system that simulates complex laser interactions thousands of times faster than conventional method...
fullText: Researchers at Stanford, UCLA, and SLAC have developed an AI system that simulates complex laser interactions thousands of times faster than conventional methods. The breakthrough allows scientists to predict how laser pulses behave inside special crystals in just milliseconds, without sacrificing much accuracy. This could dramatically improve the precision and efficiency of powerful X-ray lasers used in cutting-edge scientific research.

title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
snippet: A study of more than 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications whe...
fullText: A study of more than 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications when used for weight loss, but was associated with a higher risk of premature birth when prescribed for diabetes. The surprising difference suggests that diabetes itself may be driving the risk, although researchers caution that the drugs' safety during pregnancy remains uncertain.

title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks

fullText: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life. The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.

title: The Sun unleashed a monster storm. Earth may have made it worse

fullText: The massive solar storm that illuminated skies worldwide in May 2024 has uncovered an unexpected twist: Earth's own atmosphere may have helped make the storm so powerful. Satellite measurements revealed that roughly 85% of the charged particles fueling the disturbance originated from Earth's upper atmosphere rather than the solar wind. Scientists also detected an extraordinary 40% weakening of Earth's magnetic field high above the planet.

title: BREAKING: Most violent Godzilla film ever, Godzilla Minus Zero NOT rated ‘A’ in India despite R rating overseas; CBFC grants U/A 16+ certificate
snippet: Bollywood Hungama has been at the forefront of reporting developments surrounding the India release of Godzilla Minus Zero. In September, we spoke exclusively t...
fullText: Bollywood Hungama has been at the forefront of reporting developments surrounding the India release of Godzilla Minus Zero. In September, we spoke exclusively to Kamal Gianchandani, Chief Business Planning & Strategy at PVR INOX Limited and CEO of PVR INOX Pictures Limited, who confirmed that the much-awaited Japanese film would release in India. On November 11, we spoke to Nayana Bijli, Lead – Distribution, Licensing & Content Acquisition, PVR INOX Pictures Limited, who confirmed that Godzilla Minus Zero will indeed release in India on November 20.We have now learned that the censor process of Godzilla Minus Zero is complete. As per the website of the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), the Japanese monster flick has received a U/A 16+ rating on November 13.Interestingly, Godzilla Minus Zero received an R rating and equivalent adult classifications across most major international markets, including the USA, UK, Australia, etc., marking a rare departure for a major theatrical Godzilla entry. The R rating generated significant excitement among core fans, horror enthusiasts, and cinephiles. Fans largely celebrated the rating as proof that the makers have gone all out with the depiction of violence. With Godzilla Minus Zero not receiving an 'A' certificate in India, it now remains to be seen if the CBFC has passed the film without cuts or censored the disturbing shots.In fact, it has often happened that films that are allowed to be consumed for the under 18 population gets a harsher rating in India. A recent example was The Devil Wears Prada 2. In most countries, it was allowed to be seen for audiences of all ages. However, in India, it was passed with an 'A' rating, shocking moviegoers. Many argued that it should have got a clean 'U' rating from the CBFC.The length of Godzilla Minus Zero, as mentioned on the censor certificate, is 137.25 minutes. In other words, the film is 2 hours, 17 minutes and 35 seconds long. It'll have a release in IMAX screens in India as well.Also Read: EXCLUSIVE: Godzilla Minus Zero to FINALLY release in India on November 20; PVR INOX Pictures’ Nayana Bijli confirms IMAX release

title: Varun Dhawan to star in Yash Raj Films' first-ever horror film, set to release on March 31, 2028
snippet: Yash Raj Films (YRF) is set to venture into a new genre with its first-ever horror film, featuring Varun Dhawan in the lead role. The production house has annou...
fullText: Yash Raj Films (YRF) is set to venture into a new genre with its first-ever horror film, featuring Varun Dhawan in the lead role. The production house has announced March 31, 2028, as the worldwide theatrical release date for the untitled project, which will be directed by Rocket Boys fame Abhay Pannu.Known for backing films across genres such as romance, action, drama, comedy and thrillers, YRF is now expanding its cinematic portfolio with a theatrical horror feature. The upcoming film aims to bring the production house’s signature scale, filmmaking approach and cinematic vision to a horror experience designed specifically for the big screen.The project is being developed under the guidance of Aditya Chopra, while YRF CEO Akshaye Widhani will serve as its producer. With this film, the banner is entering theatrical horror for the first time, marking a new addition to its diverse filmography.Abhay Pannu, who gained recognition for his work on the series Rocket Boys, will not only direct the film but has also written its screenplay. The project marks his debut as a director in the theatrical feature film space. Through this collaboration, YRF continues its approach of working with emerging and unconventional storytellers while exploring different narratives within mainstream Indian cinema.For Varun Dhawan, the film marks his second collaboration with Yash Raj Films and will see him take on a genre that is different from several of his previous projects. The actor will headline the horror feature, placing him in a new cinematic space as he explores the genre under Pannu's direction.While the makers have not yet revealed the film's title or additional details about its storyline and cast, the announcement of its release date gives audiences a glimpse of YRF's upcoming plans. The film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas worldwide on March 31, 2028.With Varun Dhawan leading the project and Abhay Pannu making his theatrical directorial debut, YRF's first horror outing is among the banner's upcoming ventures to watch out for.Also Read : Kriti Sanon drops glimpse of her reunion with Bhediya team Varun Dhawan and Amar Kaushik as she lends Hindi voice for international film Obsession

title: EXCLUSIVE: Amit Sadh makes SHOCKING confession: "I don't know why certain filmmakers and casting directors are UPSET with me and why they don't give me work"
snippet: Amit Sadh has developed a loyal following thanks to his dashing looks, impressive acting talent and outspoken, no-nonsense personality off-screen. In recent yea...
fullText: Amit Sadh has developed a loyal following thanks to his dashing looks, impressive acting talent and outspoken, no-nonsense personality off-screen. In recent years, he has won appreciation for his performances in acclaimed projects like Breathe, Avrodh: The Siege Within and Jeet Ki Zid. The actor is now gearing up for the theatrical release of his upcoming film, Pratap. Interestingly, this marks his first film in a significant role in eight years to receive a proper theatrical release, the last being Gold (2018).While speaking to Amit Sadh, one can sense that he has a deep understanding about filmmaking as well. Hence, we asked him if he has a dream to make a film. Amit Sadh, in style, replied, “I have no such dream at present. My only hope is that Pratap should work. Warna jo dream leke aaye the Mumbai, woh falter ho jaayega (laughs).”He added, “On a serious note, as a creative person, you can do anything. You just need to find the right voice at the right time. Right now, I just want to do some great work and get more work. A lot of people tell me, ‘We don’t get to see you enough (in films and shows)’. Lekin main parda laga ke ghar pe nahin baitha hoon. I know the audience wants to see me. I really hope filmmakers and casting directors finally wake up and give me more work. I don’t know why they are so upset with me and why they don’t give me work. I want to work. As an actor, I am ready to do so. And I hope Pratap changes all that for me.”He signed off by stating, “Main haarne waala insaan nahin hoon. Main haarne aaya hi nahin hoon! You know me, I am a fighter. I am a gladiator. Ladte rahoonga (laughs).”Also Read: EXCLUSIVE: Amit Sadh expresses CONCERN for his co-star Tiger Shroff after shocking firing incident: “He has my wishes and prayers”

title: EXCLUSIVE: Blockbuster filmmaker Ali Abbas Zafar debuts as composer, lyricist, singer with Parivarik ManuRanjan; turns his inside joke with Ranveer Singh and Arjun Kapoor into 'Sir Sir Sir' song
snippet: Ali Abbas Zafar began his journey as a director with Mere Brother Ki Dulhan (2011) and went on to deliver memorable films like Gunday (2014), Sultan (2016), Tig...
fullText: Ali Abbas Zafar began his journey as a director with Mere Brother Ki Dulhan (2011) and went on to deliver memorable films like Gunday (2014), Sultan (2016), Tiger Zinda Hai (2017), Bharat (2019), etc. At one point, he was the only filmmaker besides Rajkumar Hirani to have two films in the coveted Rs. 300 crore club. He also made his writing debut with Mere Brother Ki Dulhan and ventured into production with Khaali Peeli (2020). His latest production, Parivarik ManuRanjan, released on Sony LIV on November 13. Interestingly, with this slice-of-life entertainer, starring Pankaj Tripathi and Aditi Rao Hydari, Ali has added another feather, or rather, feathers, to his cap.With Parivarik ManuRanjan, Ali Abbas Zafar has made his debut as a music composer. He has composed the song 'Jingle Bell' and is also one of its lyricists. For 'Sir Sir Sir', Ali has gone a step further – he is the sole composer and lyricist, and has also lent his voice to the song alongside Vishal Mishra.Bollywood Hungama exclusively spoke to Ali Abbas Zafar to understand what prompted him to take the musical plunge. Ali explained, “I have liked listening to music since childhood. Over a period of time, I have worked on films where music has been an important part of storytelling. So, I had some ideas in terms of tunes. And as they say, necessity is the mother of all inventions! The budget of this film (Parivarik ManuRanjan) was very tight. Meanwhile, I had composed a few tunes by humming or playing them on the guitar. So, I suggested a few tunes for this film. Our director, Varun V Sharma, reacted very positively to them. All those songs are now in the film.” He added, “There are three songs that I have composed.”'Jingle Bell' appears at a crucial juncture when Ranjan Dubey's (Pankaj Tripathi) life changes for the better following the entry of Manu (Aditi Rao Hydari). 'Sir Sir Sir', meanwhile, is a foot-tapping number that plays during the birthday celebrations of Ranjan's boss.Interestingly, during the promotions of Gunday (2014), Ranveer Singh, in his trademark entertaining style, had revealed that Ali Abbas Zafar had a habit of repeatedly saying “Sir Sir Sir”. When reminded of this amusing anecdote, Ali laughed and said, “Yes. It was a code word between Ranveer, Arjun Kapoor and me.”He then explained the context behind 'Sir Sir Sir', saying, “And yes, I used to say that. Go to any government office and you'll see this jargon used by employees while addressing their bosses. They don't simply say ‘sir’ when the boss instructs them or tells them something. They repeatedly say it. So, if the boss says, ‘Tomorrow, we'll have lunch together’, instead of saying, ‘Yes, sir’, the employee would say, ‘Sir, sir, sir’! If the boss instructs, ‘Shukla ki file leke aao’, the reply would be ‘Sir, sir, sir’ instead of ‘Sir, I'll get the file’.”He added, “So, it's a part of the local context. snippet: Having recently concluded its stellar series featuring music directors, singers, songwriters and audio company owners, sharing unheard and eye-opening anecdotes...
fullText: Having recently concluded its stellar series featuring music directors, singers, songwriters and audio company owners, sharing unheard and eye-opening anecdotes about everything that went into creating some of the most iconic musical chartbusters, along with underrated gems, Komal Nahta's Game Changers is back with another exciting series.Staying behind the scenes, the series is now all set to explore, perhaps, one of the most essential elements in bringing a feature film to life: the writing. After all, what would a big motion picture or a web series look like if its writing wasn't up to the mark? Be it dissecting some of the most iconic lines, the most heartwarming scenes or the story as a whole, Game Changers with Komal Nahta: The Writer Series will bring together some of the most legendary pens of Indian cinema.From the likes of Rajkumar Hirani and Abhijat Joshi (Munna Bhai M.B.B.S., Lage Raho Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, PK, Sanju, Dunki) to Javed Akhtar, the series will also feature key names like Niren Bhatt, who is making waves with his writing in the Maddock horror comedy universe (Bhediya, Munjya, Stree 2), and Sriram Raghavan (Andhaadhun, Badlapur), among others.From Juhi Chaturvedi, who has worked closely with Shoojit Sircar to create memorable scripts like Vicky Donor, Madras Cafe, Piku, October and Gulabo Sitabo, to Rumi Jaffrey, whose screenwriting credits span over three decades, the series will also feature Karan Vyas, who has been making waves with his writing prowess on OTT through projects like Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story, Scoop and Made in India: A Titan Story, among others.As has been the case with every edition so far, Komal Nahta will dive deep into engaging conversations with some of the brightest minds in the industry, who form the backbone not just of filmmaking but of the entertainment industry itself.We are all set and rolling to witness yet another special series that promises a never-before-heard deep dive into the craft of writing, exploring everything from the germ of an idea to its eventual fruition on screen.Also Read: Shaan recalls growing up in a musical family on Komal Nahta’s Game Changers: The Music Series: “ I was the weakest link to music in my family”

title: Dhindora Season 2 trailer out: Bhuvan Bam-led series to premiere on November 20; Sanjeeda Sheikh joins cast, Anup Soni, Udit Narayan and Orry make cameo appearances
snippet: Netflix has unveiled the trailer of Dhindora Season 2, bringing Bhuvan Bam back as Titu Mama and the other familiar characters from the BB Ki Vines universe. Th...
fullText: Netflix has unveiled the trailer of Dhindora Season 2, bringing Bhuvan Bam back as Titu Mama and the other familiar characters from the BB Ki Vines universe. The new season will premiere on November 20 and introduces Sanjeeda Sheikh as Kavita Mami, Titu Mama’s wife.The second season follows Titu Mama as he deals with an Rs 11 crores loss and attempts to mend his relationship with his in-laws. However, his efforts appear to lead to more complications. Alongside Titu Mama, Bhuvan will reprise his roles as Babloo ji, Janki, Sameer and Bancho.Speaking about the new season and returning to these characters, Bhuvan Bam said, “When I first created these characters, I wanted them to be outlandish yet familiar, and that remains at the heart of BB Ki Vines. Titu Mama has always had a talent for finding himself in situations he absolutely did not sign up for, and this time, he’s trying to make peace with his in-laws, which, as you can imagine, comes with its own set of complications! Partnering with Netflix has allowed us to take the BB Ki Vines universe to a much bigger canvas, where we could push our ideas further while staying true to the soul and humour of Dhindora. Season 2 takes the chaos up a notch, and I can’t wait for audiences to see Titu Mama back in action. After all, when Titu Mama is involved, peace is never really an option!”Sanjeeda Sheikh joins the cast as Kavita Mami, a character who is familiar with Titu Mama’s ways. Talking about her role, she said, “What drew me to Kavita was that she can hold her own with Titu Mama. He’s always got an explanation ready, and she’s usually the one person in the room who can see right through it. I had a lot of fun playing that equation with Bhuvan. Audiences have known Titu Mama for years, and I’m excited for them to finally meet the woman who knows him best.”The new season is directed by Sneha Shetty Kohli, who is making her directorial debut with the project. She spoke about expanding the show's setting while retaining its established humour. “One of the most exciting aspects of directing this season was bringing a fresh scale, energy and vibrancy to an already much-loved world. Making my directorial debut with this project made the experience even more special. From bizarre action sequences to colourful song-and-dance moments, every day brought something exciting. Introducing new characters and exploring their dynamics with familiar favourites was equally rewarding. Above all, capturing Bhuvan’s inimitable humour while retaining the essence of this beloved universe was an absolute joy for me.”Dhindora Season 2 is written by Bhuvan Bam, Abbas Dalal, Hussain Dalal, Chetan Dange, Gopal Dutt, Shubham Dubey and Anant Dubey. It is produced by Rohit Raj and Bhuvan Bam and will premiere on Netflix on November 20.Also Read: Bhuvan Bam begins filming for Dhindora season 2: “Nayi Chunauti, Naya Mehmaan”

title: Moushumi Chatterjee's husband Jayanta Mukherjee passes away
snippet: Veteran film producer Jayanta Mukherjee, husband of actor Moushumi Chatterjee and son of legendary singer-composer Hemant Kumar, passed away on November 12 in M...
fullText:
Veteran film producer Jayanta Mukherjee, husband of actor Moushumi Chatterjee and son of legendary singer-composer Hemant Kumar, passed away on November 12 in Mumbai. He was in his late 70s and had reportedly been unwell for some time. His demise was confirmed by BN Tiwari, President of the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE).Speaking to PTI, Tiwari said, "He passed away last evening due to age-related issues at his residence in Khar."According to reports, Jayanta died at his residence after his health deteriorated. He had reportedly been dealing with age-related ailments for some time. The family has not yet shared a detailed public statement regarding his demise.
Jayanta Mukherjee's association with films and television
Jayanta Mukherjee worked behind the scenes in the entertainment industry as a film producer. His production credits included Mazaaq (1975), Do Ladke Dono Kadke (1979) and Biwi Aur Makan (1966). Both Mazaaq and Do Ladke Dono Kadke featured Moushumi Chatterjee in prominent roles. He was also associated with the television serial Talaash, which aired in 1992.Coming from a family with a strong musical background, Jayanta was the son of Hemant Kumar, one of the most recognised singers and music composers in Indian cinema. He also had an association with the music department of Biwi Aur Makan.
Jayanta Mukherjee and Moushumi Chatterjee's family
Jayanta and Moushumi Chatterjee got married in 1972 and shared more than five decades together. The couple had two daughters, Payal and Megha. Their elder daughter, Payal Mukherjee, passed away in December 2019 at the age of 45 following health complications.Jayanta is survived by his wife, Moushumi and younger daughter Megha.Also Read: Moushumi Chatterjee breaks silence on retirement speculation, reveals why she took a long break: “Who said I am retiring?”

title: Aditi Rao Hydari reveals the family tradition she shares with husband Siddharth: “It's common that everyone laughs together”
snippet: In an exclusive interview with Filmfare, Aditi Rao Hydari opened up about the values and traditions that hold a special place in her family and that of her husb...
fullText: In an exclusive interview with Filmfare, Aditi Rao Hydari opened up about the values and traditions that hold a special place in her family and that of her husband, Siddharth. The actor spoke about how simple everyday moments, including sharing laughter and meals, help bring family members closer and create a sense of togetherness.qsazTalking about one tradition that is common to both families, Aditi revealed that they believe in finding reasons to laugh together, regardless of the circumstances. She said, “I think in our family, with Siddharth and in his family as well, it's common that everyone laughs together. No matter what happens, to find something to laugh about, I like that a lot.”The actor further explained that maintaining a sense of humour becomes particularly important when families go through challenging situations. According to her, being able to find something positive even during difficult moments can help people stay connected. Elaborating on this, she added, “Sometimes, if something is difficult, or if there's a problem in the family, no matter what happens, at the end of the day, to be able to find something to smile about, something to laugh about.”Aditi also spoke about the role food plays in bringing people together. Agreeing with a thought shared by Pankaj Tripathi, she highlighted how sitting down for a meal and sharing food can create a sense of belonging, even among people who are not related by blood. She said, “I heard this from someone else as well, that eating together, the food that people sit together and share, whether it's your team or a family of blood, it becomes a family. Very true. So, that eating and sharing food is very, very important.”Through her observations, Aditi emphasised that family bonds are often strengthened through small, everyday gestures. For her, laughing together during difficult times and making time to share meals are among the simple ways people can build meaningful relationships. Her thoughts also reflect how family extends beyond blood relations and is shaped by shared experiences, affection and companionship.Meanwhile, Aditi will next be seen in Parivarik ManuRanjan, which premiered on SonyLIV from today November 13. title: Netflix announces Pushpak Vimaan: Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee, and Barun Sobti headline Sudip Sharma’s new crime comedy
snippet: Netflix has announced Pushpak Vimaan, a new crime caper created by Sudip Sharma, known for helming some of India's acclaimed crime dramas. The upcoming series w...
fullText: Netflix has announced Pushpak Vimaan, a new crime caper created by Sudip Sharma, known for helming some of India's acclaimed crime dramas. The upcoming series will feature Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti in lead roles and marks a departure from the intense storytelling style associated with Sharma, as he explores comedy through an ensemble of eccentric characters and unpredictable situations.Co-created and written by Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee, Pushpak Vimaan is produced by Film Squad Productions LLP. The series revolves around a crime caper in which humour emerges from an eclectic mix of characters and a chain of events that gradually spirals beyond everyone's control.Speaking about the project, creator and director Sudip Sharma said, “With Pushpak Vimaan, I wanted to explore a very different creative space. It is a crime caper, but one in which the humour comes from the characters, their circumstances and the sheer unpredictability of the situations they find themselves in. Netflix is where I choose to experiment, and it was the natural home for a story of this nature. It provided the space to explore the genre freely and to bring this unusual ensemble of characters to life.”Tanya Bami, Series Head, Netflix India, also expressed excitement about the collaboration, highlighting the platform's continued association with the filmmaker. She said, "Pushpak Vimaan is a show we are very excited to announce. Firstly this is our next franchise with Sudip Sharma whose distinct style of combining a compelling story with a deep commentary on society has always found critical as well as audience love. With Pushpak Vimaan, we’re happy to champion Sudip’s creativity once again, this time with a comedy series he wrote, showran and directed and it’s an unputdownable caper. It’s one hell of a fun ride that we can’t wait for our audiences to experience."Pushpak Vimaan marks the second creative collaboration between Sudip Sharma and Netflix, following their association on Kohrra. With the new series, the filmmaker ventures into a different genre while bringing together three familiar faces from the streaming space.The series is directed by Sudip Sharma, with Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee credited as its creators and writers. title: Kareena Kapoor Khan faces legal notice over Quranic verse on 30-carat emerald pendant worn for Diwali 2026
snippet: Kareena Kapoor Khan's Diwali 2026 appearance has sparked a controversy over the 30-carat emerald pendant she wore as part of her festive look. The jewellery pie...
fullText: Kareena Kapoor Khan's Diwali 2026 appearance has sparked a controversy over the 30-carat emerald pendant she wore as part of her festive look. The jewellery piece, reportedly a 200-year-old heirloom belonging to the erstwhile royal family of Bhopal, features the Quranic verse Ayat-ul-Kursi. The controversy has led Congress spokesperson Abbas Hafeez to issue a legal notice seeking the removal of the actress's photographs from social media and a public apology. Meanwhile, the Hindu Utsav Samiti has come out in support of Kareena.The actress's festive look featured a silver kaftan paired with a matching turban and the statement emerald pendant. While her outfit and jewellery caught the attention of social media users, the religious inscription on the heirloom soon became a subject of debate. The pendant is associated with the Begums of Bhopal and has reportedly been passed down through Saif Ali Khan's family.Stylist Rhea Kapoor shared details about Kareena's appearance in a social media post, explaining the history and significance of the pieces she wore. Describing the ensemble, she wrote, "Real movie star, real chandi, real heirlooms and real personal style. Kareena in a pure chandi kaftan and turban by @punit.balana,wearing a 200-year-old kalgi from the Nawab of Bhopal and the Begum of Bhopal’s 30-carat emerald, carved with the Ayat-ul-Kursi. Outfit: @punitbalanaofficial Jewelry: Heirlooms of the Bhopal royal family, Kareena’s own. These pieces come through Saif’s family: his grandmother, Sajida Sultan, was the daughter of the last ruling Nawab of Bhopal."However, Abbas Hafeez objected to the use of the Quranic verse as part of a fashion accessory. According to him, the pendant represents the Islamic heritage of the Begums of Bhopal and was commissioned as an expression of religious faith rather than for fashion purposes.Clarifying his position, Hafeez said that his objection was not related to Kareena celebrating Diwali or choosing to wear a particular outfit. He told FPJ, "Let me make it very clear: people are free to celebrate whichever festival they wish and wear whatever clothes they want. Our objection is only to the Quranic verse. Even if she had worn it on Eid, it would still have been objectionable," he said.Advocate Mohammad Zafar further explained that the legal notice demands the removal of Kareena's social media photographs. He also stated that if the request is not addressed, further legal remedies could be considered. While the controversy continues to draw attention, the Hindu Utsav Samiti's support for the actress has added another dimension to the debate surrounding her Diwali appearance.Also Read : Saif Ali Khan shares first fitness video, Kareena Kapoor Khan REACTS

title: SCOOP: Hanuman Ansh makers hit JACKPOT yet again; Sony acquires OTT and satellite rights for a WHOPPING Rs. 63 cr
snippet: The box office performance of Hanuman Ansh has stunned one and all in the trade and industry. The film was released in cinemas on August 7 and initially struggl...
fullText: The box office performance of Hanuman Ansh has stunned one and all in the trade and industry. The film was released in cinemas on August 7 and initially struggled to attract footfalls. However, its fortunes changed dramatically in the third week, following which it exploded at the box office in its fourth and fifth weeks. Despite stiff competition from Toxic and Mirzapur The Movie, Hanuman Ansh continued to thrive in cinemas. Ultimately, the film, made on a very modest budget, went on to collect more than Rs. 300 crores at the box office. Usually, films premiere on OTT around eight weeks after their theatrical release. However, Hanuman Ansh enjoyed an extended run in theatres, and hence, the makers took their time bringing the film to streaming. More than three-and-a-half months after its theatrical release, Hanuman Ansh will finally be available on Sony LIV. The makers recently announced that the devotional film will premiere on Sony LIV on November 27, followed by its television premiere on Sony MAX soon.Bollywood Hungama has learned that the makers have been paid handsomely for the film's post-theatrical rights. A source told Bollywood Hungama, “Sony has picked up the digital and television rights of Hanuman Ansh for a price of Rs. 63 crores. It's a huge amount, but then Hanuman Ansh is no small film either. It attracted audiences across the country – from single screens to multiplexes, from megacities to the smallest of villages. There's a huge section of the audience that is yet to watch the film, while many may want to watch it again. Hence, the team at Sony is confident that Hanuman Ansh will receive huge viewership on both digital and satellite. That's why they feel justified in acquiring the rights at such a price.”Yesterday, Bollywood Hungama also broke the news that a grand success bash will be held in Mumbai in a few days. We carried the quote of a source who told us, “The success party of Hanuman Ansh will take place over the weekend in Mumbai. The entire team of the film, including the producers, director Vishal Chaturvedi and the star cast, will be present in full force. Representatives of Cinepolis India, which distributed the film, will also be in attendance. After all, they played an important role in the film's success by ensuring that it received a proper theatrical release.”The source continued, “However, this won't be your typical film success bash. Interestingly, no alcohol or non-vegetarian food will be served at the party. Instead, guests will be treated to pure vegetarian, satvik food, in keeping with the beliefs of the team and the spiritual theme of Hanuman Ansh. The makers want the celebration to reflect the values and sentiments associated with the film.”

title: SHOCKING: Amitabh Bachchan's Jalsa at centre of family DISPUTE; sister-in-law Ramola challenges gift deed transferring iconic bungalow to Jaya Bachchan
snippet: A property dispute involving Amitabh Bachchan's iconic Jalsa bungalow in Mumbai has come to light. According to a report in Mumbai Mirror, the superstar's siste...
fullText: A property dispute involving Amitabh Bachchan's iconic Jalsa bungalow in Mumbai has come to light. According to a report in Mumbai Mirror, the superstar's sister-in-law, Ramola Bachchan, has challenged a gift deed executed in 1993, through which ownership of the property was transferred to Jaya Bachchan.Ramola, the wife of Amitabh's brother Ajitabh Bachchan, has reportedly filed multiple complaints with registration authorities over the past seven months. She claims that she was neither aware of nor had consented to the transaction. The matter is currently under examination by the authorities.As per Mumbai Mirror, Jalsa was originally recorded in Ramola's name before being transferred to Jaya's name. The dispute resurfaced following alleged attempts to remove Ramola's name from the government's Property Card and replace it with Jaya's. Interestingly, while records of Kapol Housing Society reportedly show Jaya as the owner, the Property Card continues to carry Ramola's name.The report further states that questions have been raised about the manner in which the 1993 gift deed was executed. According to the complaints, the document was prepared on plain paper without stamp duty being paid at the time and allegedly did not have witnesses. Ramola has also questioned its subsequent registration and regularization under the Abhay Yojana scheme.The matter has now reached the office of the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Andheri. Confirming receipt of the complaint, Deputy Registrar Faiyaz Mulani told Mumbai Mirror that a hearing had been initiated and the other parties had been asked to submit their responses.Jalsa, one of Mumbai's most famous celebrity residences, has been associated with Amitabh Bachchan for decades. Jalsa was originally named Mansa and was owned by producer N C Sippy. As per reports, it is said that it was given to Amitabh Bachchan as remuneration for his 1982 film, Satte Pe Satta. The superstar has previously spoken about purchasing, selling and later reacquiring the property.Meanwhile, Amitabh Bachchan did not respond to Mumbai Mirror's queries. Jaya Bachchan could not be reached, while a spokesperson for Abhishek Bachchan declined to comment, describing it as an internal family issue.The allegations remain disputed, and the authorities are yet to determine the validity of the documents and ownership-related claims.Also Read: Amitabh Bachchan opens up about discomfort in hand amid KBC 18 absence: “I have been experiencing some discomfort in the hand I use for writing”

In a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter India, Karan opened up about the trolling directed at the couples, expressing his reservations about audiences analysing their relationships and making unsolicited comments about their personal lives.Recalling the backlash that followed the premiere episode of Koffee With Karan 8, which featured Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone together for the first time on the celebrity chat show, Karan maintained that the couple was simply being honest about their relationship. fullText: Ranveer Singh’s maternal grandfather, Dr Ram Hingorani, passed away on Diwali at the age of 96. She also posted several photographs and videos featuring her grandfather, offering a glimpse into their time together.Announcing his demise, Saumya revealed that Dr Ram passed away peacefully during Lakshmi Puja on Diwali. In her tribute, she wrote, “My Dadu, Dr. Ram, peacefully left us on Diwali to go home to my Dadi. He couldn’t have picked a more auspicious time – the golden hour of the day, during Lakshmi Puja.”She further expressed her thoughts about her grandparents reuniting, adding, “I bet the two of them are in their chairs sipping on a crisp whiskey, enjoying watching us together."Saumya began her note by remembering the 96 years he had lived, writing, “96 years young. A glorious life to be celebrated, not mourned." She also thanked him for being the “best Dadu in the world” and concluded her tribute with a heartfelt message, “Save a scoop of ice cream for me. Until we dance again. Hari Om.”Meanwhile, Ranveer Singh and his wife, Deepika Padukone, have not publicly shared a statement about the loss so far.Ranveer Singh’s bond with his maternal grandfatherRanveer has frequently shared moments with his maternal grandfather on social media, giving fans a glimpse into their relationship. He captioned the picture, “Nana-G."Their bond was also evident during the promotions of Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani in August 2023. Ranveer shared a series of photographs and videos featuring his grandfather, who was 93 at the time. One of the videos showed the two dancing together to the song ‘Jhumka Gira Re’.Through these posts, Ranveer had offered glimpses of the special place his grandfather held in his life. title: Nora Fatehi’s appearance in Sukesh Chandrashekhar Case comes under scrutiny as defence prepares for cross-examination
snippet: Nora Fatehi appeared before the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi on Wednesday as a prosecution witness in the Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing (EOW) case against ...
fullText: Nora Fatehi appeared before the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi on Wednesday as a prosecution witness in the Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing (EOW) case against Sukesh Chandrashekhar. Her appearance before Additional Sessions Judge Gagandeep Singh came after the court had summoned her twice. On an earlier date, Fatehi had sought exemption from appearing, following which the court reportedly expressed displeasure over her absence and cautioned her, saying, “Don’t take the court for granted.” According to the defence, proceedings were also delayed on Wednesday before she arrived.The same story, untestedDuring her deposition, Fatehi reportedly reiterated her account that she had been engaged as an artiste for a charity event in Chennai in December 2020 and had not received any payment for it. However, the defence has questioned this version, pointing to her earlier statements to investigating agencies, as reported in the media, concerning a luxury handbag, a phone and a BMW car allegedly linked to the same event.The defence maintains that these aspects have not yet been examined through cross-examination and will be raised during the proceedings.A witness today is not immune tomorrowFatehi's team has maintained that she is appearing in the matter only as a witness. Responding to this, the defence has referred to Section 319 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), which allows a trial court to proceed against another person, including someone appearing as a witness, if evidence presented during the trial indicates their involvement in an offence.In a statement, Advocate Anant Malik, counsel for Sukesh Chandrashekhar, said, “Nobody disputes that Ms. Fatehi has been summoned as a witness. But a summons is not a certificate of innocence, and it is certainly not a licence to treat the Court’s time as optional. The Hon’ble Court itself had to remind her not to take it for granted. What the public has heard today is a handful of rehearsed lines. Cross-examination is where that story will be tested. The defence will place documents and material before the Hon’ble Court, and if that material shows her role was larger than she admits, we will seek appropriate orders, strictly in accordance with law, including under Section 319 CrPC. Celebrity or not, every witness stands equal before the law.”The defence further stated that it has full faith in the court and the trial process, adding that its arguments will be presented through evidence and cross-examination. The statement was issued by the office of Advocate Anant Malik, who represents Sukesh Chandrashekhar in the case.Also Read : Nora Fatehi summoned as witness in Sukesh Chandrashekhar Rs. 200 crore extortion case; court grants exemption, sets November 6 hearing

fullText: It’s the season of sequels where even older films are converted into franchises. The recent successful example of the same was the Emraan Hashmi-starrer Awarapan 2. title: Ahaan Panday’s Beparwah co-star, Aaishvary Thackeray, loses Rs. 19,000 to cyber fraud; files police complaint
snippet: Cybercrime is on the rise, and not just the common man, but even those associated with the film industry and politics are falling prey to it. The latest promine...
fullText: Cybercrime is on the rise, and not just the common man, but even those associated with the film industry and politics are falling prey to it. The latest prominent personality to become a victim is Aaishvary Thackeray, the grandson of Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray. As per reports, he has lodged a police complaint after money was fraudulently debited from his bank account.According to a report in The Times of India, Aaishvary Thackeray revealed that he lives with his mother, Smita, and grandmother, Kunda. He was at his residence in Andheri on October 30 when, at around 1:30 am, he received a text message informing him that Rs. 307.82 had been deducted from his bank account. Eight minutes later, he received another message notifying him of a further deduction of Rs. 15,511.98. Four more fraudulent transactions followed, taking the total amount lost to cyber fraud to Rs. 19,638.15.Hence, Aaishvary Thackeray visited Oshiwara police station and filed a complaint. The Times of India report confirmed that the cops have begun investigating and have found that the transactions had been made overseas. The article also said that an FIR was registered against an unknown cyber fraudster under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Information Technology Act.About Aaishvary ThackerayAaishvary Thackeray, 30, worked as an assistant director on Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Bajirao Mastani (2015), starring Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone and Priyanka Chopra. Last year, he made his debut as an actor in Anurag Kashyap’s two-part crime comedy saga, Nishaanchi (2025). Aaishvary played a double role in his debut venture and was quite appreciated.Besides acting, Aaishvary Thackeray also has an interest in music. In Nishaanchi's first part, he composed and wrote the song 'Pigeon Kabootar' and sang 'Neend Bhi Teri'. In the second part, he composed the 'End Theme'.In the 2026 YRF (Yash Raj Films) Spy film, Alpha, starring Alia Bhatt and Sharvari, Aaishvary was one of the music programmers on the song 'Massacre', 'Champagne', 'Haaniya' and 'Agni'. He was also one of the lyricists of 'Massacre - Midnight Version'.Aaishvary Thackeray will next be seen as an actor in Beparwah, which marks Ahaan Panday’s second film after the sleeper blockbuster Saiyaara (2025). Besides Aaishvary and Ahaan, it also stars Sharvari, Bobby Deol and Jimmy Sheirgill. Directed by Ali Abbas Zafar, it releases in cinemas on March 26, 2027.Also Read: Aaishvary Thackeray replaces Babil Khan in Hindi remake of Telugu blockbuster Baby

title: Amitabh Bachchan wins personality rights case; Delhi High Court passes final decree after four defendants settle
snippet: The Delhi High Court has passed a final decree in favour of Amitabh Bachchan in his personality rights case, restraining several entities and unidentified perso...
fullText:
The Delhi High Court has passed a final decree in favour of Amitabh Bachchan in his personality rights case, restraining several entities and unidentified persons from commercially using his name, image, voice or likeness without his consent. The order was passed by Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav, concluding proceedings that began with an interim injunction in November 2022.The Court held that the right to control the commercial use of an individual's identity falls under the “right to publicity”. It observed that Bachchan's name and photographs had been used without permission in ways that could falsely suggest his endorsement of products or services.The actor had approached the Court over the alleged unauthorised use of his identity across different platforms and merchandise. These included a mobile application titled Amitabh Bachchan Video Call, messages promoting a purported Kaun Banega Crorepati lottery, a general knowledge quiz book featuring his photograph, T-shirts, posters and domain names incorporating his identity.The Court noted that the unauthorised use involved Bachchan's “very name and photographs” and found that the requirements for protecting his publicity rights had been met.
Protection extended to unidentified persons
The final decree also covers unidentified individuals, commonly referred to as John Does. The Court took note of the continued use of Bachchan's persona through anonymous websites, applications, posters and messaging platforms, observing that those responsible may not always be identifiable.Four defendants, Rajat Nagi, Manoj Publications, Tamatina and Mahesh Patel, settled the matter with Bachchan and acknowledged his publicity and privacy rights. As part of the settlement, the defendants agreed to discontinue the use of his identity. The commitments included deleting the video-call application, stopping publication of the quiz book and sale of posters, and deleting the domain name amitabhbachchan.in.The remaining defendants did not appear before the Court or file written statements despite being served. The Court held that the case did not involve disputed facts requiring a trial and granted a summary judgment against them. It also clarified that Bachchan could initiate fresh proceedings if further unauthorised use of his persona occurs.The November 2022 interim injunction now stands merged with the final decree.Also Read: Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu bungalow Jalsa among locations named in bomb threat email: Report

title: Bombay High Court grants interim relief to Naagzilla consultant Kuldeep Singh Champawat in Rs. 3.92 cr financial irregularity case; no role attributed to him in payment hierarchy
snippet: The Bombay High Court has granted interim protection to Kuldeep Singh Champawat, a consultant associated with Kartik Aaryan-starrer Naagzilla, in a case involvi...
fullText:
The Bombay High Court has granted interim protection to Kuldeep Singh Champawat, a consultant associated with Kartik Aaryan-starrer Naagzilla, in a case involving alleged financial irregularities amounting to approximately Rs. 3.92 crore. The matter concerns alleged violations of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) agreed upon between Dharma Productions Private Limited and Mahaveer Jain Films Private Limited.The order was passed by Justice Prafulla S. Khubalkar on November 3, 2026, while hearing Champawat's anticipatory bail application. The case follows an FIR registered at Mumbai's D.N. Nagar Police Station on September 26, 2026.According to the complaint, payments worth Rs. 3,92,76,308 were allegedly made without following the financial procedures outlined in the SOP signed by the two production companies.
What is the allegation against Kuldeep Singh Champawat?
During the hearing, advocate Niteen Pradhan, representing Champawat, argued that his client was working only as a consultant and did not have the authority to approve or release payments. He further submitted that financial decisions were handled by chartered accountants and that Champawat was not included in the designated payment approval hierarchy.After considering the submissions, the High Court observed that the payment approval structure did not assign Champawat any specific role in authorising the payments. The court also took note of the fact that he had no criminal antecedents.
Court directs Champawat to cooperate with investigation
While granting protection, the High Court directed Champawat to appear before the D.N. Nagar Police Station on November 12, 2026, between 10 am and 2 pm. He has also been asked to cooperate with the investigation and provide relevant documents whenever required by the investigating authorities.The case relates to financial transactions between the two production houses associated with Naagzilla. The court's order concerns Champawat's anticipatory bail plea and the conditions attached to the interim protection. The investigation into the alleged financial irregularities is ongoing.Also Read: Naagzilla producers take legal action over alleged Rs. 3.92 crores misappropriation; Mumbai court rejects anticipatory bail pleas of 3 production executives

title: Priyanka Chopra Jonas announces Ventilator 2, reunites with director Rajesh Mapuskar; film set for 2027 release
snippet: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has announced the sequel to her 2016 Marathi film Ventilator, titled Ventilator 2. The upcoming project will be produced under her banner ...
fullText:
Priyanka Chopra Jonas has announced the sequel to her 2016 Marathi film Ventilator, titled Ventilator 2. The upcoming project will be produced under her banner Purple Pebble Pictures and will see her reunite with filmmaker Rajesh Mapuskar, who returns as the writer and director. The film is scheduled to release in 2027, while details about its cast and storyline are yet to be revealed.Announcing the project on Instagram, Priyanka looked back at the original film and spoke about its significance in her journey as a producer. She also reflected on the vision behind Purple Pebble Pictures, which was established to support stories with meaningful narratives.Sharing the announcement, she wrote, “10 years ago, with @purplepebblepictures, I decided I want to tell stories that mean something. Ventilator was one of those very important stories to us at the company. A decade later, we’re coming back to it, with so much more…” 
View this post on Instagram
 
A post shared by Priyanka (@priyankachopra)Priyanka Chopra Jonas reunites with Rajesh Mapuskar
Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Dr Madhu Chopra, and Rajesh Mapuskar will produce Ventilator 2 under the banners of Purple Pebble Pictures and Magij Pictures. The reunion brings back the filmmaker who directed the original, which received three National Film Awards.Released in 2016, Ventilator revolved around the Kamerkar family, whose members come together at a hospital after an elderly family member is placed on a ventilator just before Ganesh Chaturthi. The Marathi film explored family relationships, generational differences and unresolved tensions through a combination of humour and emotional moments.Mapuskar received the National Film Award for Best Director, while the film also won awards for Best Editing and Best Sound Mixing.
A decade of Purple Pebble Pictures
Founded by Priyanka, Purple Pebble Pictures has backed projects across different languages and genres. Its filmography includes Pahuna: The Little Visitors, Paani, The Sky Is Pink, The White Tiger, Firebrand, To Kill a Tiger and Anuja.With Ventilator 2, the production house returns to one of its early projects, bringing Priyanka and Mapuskar together for another chapter. Further details about the film's production and cast are awaited.Also Read: Priyanka Chopra’s National award winning film Ventilator is now a Gujarati play and here are the details

title: Delhi High Court rules Doosra infringed Sourav Ganguly's personality rights, directs makers to deposit Rs. 2 crores
snippet: The Delhi High Court has ruled that the film Doosra infringed upon former Indian cricket captain Sourav Ganguly’s personality and publicity rights. In its direc...
fullText:
The Delhi High Court has ruled that the film Doosra infringed upon former Indian cricket captain Sourav Ganguly’s personality and publicity rights. In its directions, the Court has ordered the film's makers, Ramesh Deo Productions Private Limited, to deposit Rs. 2 crore and display disclaimers in both Hindi and English at the beginning and end of the film.The ruling comes in connection with a lawsuit filed by Sourav Ganguly along with Luv Films over the unauthorised use of his identity and life events in the film. The Court has also restrained the makers from releasing Doosra on OTT platforms or through any other medium.According to the Court's observations, elements of Ganguly's personality and incidents from his life are closely connected to the film's narrative. This makes it difficult to remove the portions in question from the final cut. The Court, therefore, directed the makers to include prominent disclaimers to clarify the nature of the film's association with the former cricketer.The disclaimers must explicitly state that Ganguly did not give consent for the commercial use or depiction of his persona in the film. They must also clarify that the project does not have any official association or authorisation from him.
Sourav Ganguly's personality rights case and the upcoming biopic
The ruling brings attention to the legal issues surrounding the use of public figures' identities and personal histories in films and other commercial projects. Personality rights generally protect individuals against the unauthorised commercial exploitation of aspects such as their name, image and likeness.Meanwhile, Sourav Ganguly's authorised biographical film, Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story, is also in the works. Directed by Vikramaditya Motwane and produced by Luv Ranjan and Ankur Garg, the project is scheduled for release on May 14, 2026.Also Read: Rajkummar Rao, Ankur Garg celebrate Mahashtami with Sourav Ganguly ahead of Dada biopic

title: Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu bungalow Jalsa among locations named in bomb threat email: Report
snippet: Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu residence, Jalsa, was among several prominent locations in Mumbai mentioned in a bomb threat email received by the authorities. Followin...
fullText: Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu residence, Jalsa, was among several prominent locations in Mumbai mentioned in a bomb threat email received by the authorities. Following the alert, security agencies conducted searches at the locations named in the message. However, no suspicious objects were found during the investigation. The latest threat comes amid increased security concerns in Mumbai, particularly following recent incidents involving Bollywood personalities. Bachchan’s security arrangements had also been strengthened last week.Amitabh Bachchan’s bungalow named in bomb threat emailAccording to ANI, Mumbai authorities received a bomb threat email that reportedly mentioned the Bombay High Court, Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Mahalaxmi Racecourse and Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu bungalow, Jalsa. Following the threat, security personnel immediately initiated searches at the premises identified in the email.Bomb Detection and Disposal Squads (BDDS) carried out thorough inspections of the locations. However, police officials confirmed that nothing suspicious was discovered during the searches, bringing some relief amid the security alert.Amitabh Bachchan’s security heightened following earlier threatThis is not the first time Bachchan’s residence has been mentioned in a bomb threat. On Friday, October 23, the Mumbai mayor’s office reportedly received a similar threat email that named the actor’s Juhu residence, the mayor’s office and Mahalaxmi Racecourse. The racecourse is also scheduled to host singer-actor Diljit Dosanjh’s performance on November 27.Following the earlier alert, security arrangements outside Jalsa were strengthened on October 25, when Bachchan continued his customary Sunday meeting with fans. The actor also maintained the tradition on November 1, but with additional precautions. He greeted admirers from behind a transparent bulletproof enclosure, accompanied by his son Abhishek Bachchan, while security personnel monitored the gathering.The latest threat comes amid increased attention on the safety of Bollywood personalities following a firing incident in Juhu earlier this month.Meanwhile, Bachchan recently shared an update about his health and recovery. In a post on his Tumblr blog, the actor indicated that he needed more rest. He wrote, “Yet more rest needed .. adjusting .. thinking and wondering .. the human body and its uniqueness.”Tiger Shroff firing incident adds to security concernsOn October 18, two men opened fire at Tiger Shroff’s car near a football ground in Juhu. While the actor escaped unharmed, his driver and another person were reportedly injured in the incident.Following the firing, three suspects were arrested in Kota, Rajasthan, and subsequently handed over to the Mumbai Police for further investigation. The incident, along with the recent threat emails, has brought security arrangements around prominent Bollywood personalities into focus.Also Read :

title: Claves | De un nuevo impuesto a los grandes empresarios a la “unión de la amistad”: el programa del PSOE para el 29-N
snippet: El PSOE ha presentado este domingo su programa de Gobierno de cara a las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre. El documento, de 114 páginas, recoge 500 “compr...
fullText: El PSOE ha presentado este domingo su programa de Gobierno de cara a las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre. El documento, de 114 páginas, recoge 500 “compromisos” de Pedro Sánchez, incluido destinar el 1% del PIB a vivienda social, crear una prestación estatal por crianza, un nuevo impuesto “contra la especulación” de los fondos buitre y grandes propietarios, y un impulso de las renovables para alcanzar el 81% de generación eléctrica en 2030. El texto también contempla un nuevo impuesto a los grandes empresarios que cobren más de 100 veces el sueldo de sus empleados y promete el reconocimiento de la “unión de la amistad” para dotar de “un amparo legal” a las “situaciones en las que personas unidas por un vínculo de amistad deciden asumir un compromiso mutuo de cuidados”. La lista incluye además un “escaño ciudadano” en las Cortes Generales y propuestas que no lograron salir adelante esta legislatura, como la Ley de Trata y una Ley Abolicionista del Sistema Prostitucional o la prohibición del uso de las redes sociales a los menores de 16 años.Seguir leyendo

fullText: Alberto Núñez Feijóo continúa con sus críticas contra el PSOE —que “va como pollo sin cabeza”— conforme avanza la campaña y las encuestas confirman la pugna de los dos principales partidos por el primer puesto ante el 29-N. “¿Por qué ha adelantado [las elecciones]? Porque está muerto de miedo, por el calvario judicial que le espera”, ha lanzado el líder del PP contra el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, este domingo en Santander. Allí, Feijóo ha reunido a los principales cargos del Partido Popular de Asturias, de Cantabria y de País Vasco. Todo, un día después de que el candidato al Congreso por Guipuzkoa, Jon Echevarría, denunciase a través de un vídeo una agresión sufrida en Hernani junto a otros compañeros de Nuevas Generaciones.Seguir leyendo

title: Abascal vincula inmigración y delincuencia con datos falsos sobre la población extranjera de Cornellà
snippet: El líder de Vox y candidato a la presidencia del Gobierno, Santiago Abascal, ha aportado este domingo, en un mitin en Cataluña, datos falsos para vincular, una ...
fullText: El líder de Vox y candidato a la presidencia del Gobierno, Santiago Abascal, ha aportado este domingo, en un mitin en Cataluña, datos falsos para vincular, una vez más, migración e inseguridad. El partido ultra ha elegido Cornellà de Llobregat, municipio del cinturón industrial de Barcelona de voto socialista, para azuzar el miedo a los extranjeros. “Los españoles son minoría en Cornellà. Rechazamos la invasión migratoria, la ilegalidad y a los delincuentes y a los políticos traidores que les han regalado lo que es nuestro”. Según el Instituto de Estadística de Cataluña (Idescat), sin embargo, en enero de 2025 vivían en Cornellà 92.255 vecinos, de los que más del 81% son de nacionalidad española.Seguir leyendo

title: Sergio Ramírez ingresa en la RAE: “Perdí un país, pero nunca he sido extranjero en España”
snippet: “Al volver la vista atrás, queda el camino azaroso. Cuesta arriba, cuesta abajo, subidas y caídas, vueltas y revueltas, destierros, una patria perdida, otra gan...
fullText: “Al volver la vista atrás, queda el camino azaroso. Cuesta arriba, cuesta abajo, subidas y caídas, vueltas y revueltas, destierros, una patria perdida, otra ganada, es la reflexión que hago sobre mi vida al entrar en esta casa de la lengua. Acogido, amparado, reconfortado, bajo la certidumbre de que, si algo no he perdido entre tantas vicisitudes, es esa lengua”. El escritor Sergio Ramírez (Masatepe, Nicaragua, 84 años) recordaba a su “maestro literario, José Coronel Urtecho, sentado en el corredor de la hacienda Las Brisas en la frontera entre Costa Rica y Nicaragua”, recitando en griego versos una Ilíada con la que compara su propia vida. Premio Cervantes en 2017, luchador de la primera hora del sandinismo y exvicepresidente de Nicaragua, se exilió en España en 2021 y en 2023 el régimen de Ortega le despojó de su nacionalidad. Esta tarde, en la Real Academia Española, ha ingresado como miembro en la silla L, que dejó vacante al morir otro de sus maestros, Mario Vargas Llosa, a quien ha dedicado su discurso de ingreso, titulado Un novelista ecuménico.Seguir leyendo

title: “Os deseo sufrimiento”: gloria y caída de Jensen Huang, rey de Nvidia, verso salvaje de la IA
snippet: Jensen Huang es el protagonista de una historia imposible, una de esas epopeyas de superación y gloria que han ayudado a cimentar el mito estadounidense de las ...
fullText: Jensen Huang es el protagonista de una historia imposible, una de esas epopeyas de superación y gloria que han ayudado a cimentar el mito estadounidense de las oportunidades, de país joven, rico y salvaje donde todo es posible con esfuerzo. Nacido en Taiwán en 1963, llegó a los nueve años a Estados Unidos junto a su hermano, como menor no acompañado, con el fin de reunirse con un tío que vivía en el Estado de Washington, pero que lo internó por error en una academia para chicos problemáticos en Kentucky. Los padres lograron emigrar a los dos años y la familia se reunió en Oregón, donde Jensen destacó en los estudios y logró su primer empleo sirviendo mesas en la cadena de comida rápida Denny’s. Se graduó en ingeniería eléctrica dos años antes de lo habitual. En la universidad conoció a Lori Mills, una de las pocas chicas que estudiaban esa carrera, y se casaron.Seguir leyendo
